messages:
Sam: Quick sync — I'm pushing a prototype for per-token SLI buckets to the cost dashboard. Goal: show 50/90/99 latency percentiles and amortized token cost by route + model tier. Curious about how we want to include cache savings in the single-number SLI
Mira: Nice. Are we talking raw token-burn or effective cost after cache/fuzzy hits?
Sam: Effective cost after cache. We want the UI to reflect 'net token-equivalent cost' so customers see what they actually pay. But telemetry right now emits token_count and cache_hit=true/false, not an amortized credit amount per request.
Jordan: That makes sense. Two problems: 1) cache credits are often per-session/prefix and 2) sampling rate for high-volume routes is 1% — noisy for 99th perc.
Alex: For 1) we can emit a small field cache_credit_applied that is the token-equivalent saved on that response (int). For 2) we should bucket-aggregate on the ingest side to avoid needing full fidelity.
Mira: I like emitting cache_credit_applied. But how do we avoid double-counting when a cached prefix is served across models (route switched)?
Sam: Proposal: include route_id and model_variant_id in the telemetry envelope, and add a lineage_id for the cached prefix. Then ingestion can attribute credit to the route that warmed the cache via last-writer-window heuristic.
Jordan: Lineage_id will increase cardinality a lot. How big will that table be in ClickHouse?
Alex: We can hash lineage_id and sample at ingest for hot prefixes only. For billing-facing panels we can run an offline reconciliation job that processes full logs for the last 7 days and backfills precise credits for top N prefixes.
Mira: UX question — do we show an "amortized cache credit" toggle per dashboard card? I worry non-technical PMs will be confused by two numbers.
Sam: Yeah: default card = effective cost (amortized credits applied). Secondary tooltip = breakdown: raw token burn, cache credit, model-sku multiplier, quantization factor.
Jordan: On sampling: for tails we may need to temporarily bump sampling for flagged routes during canary windows. ops-bot: sampling-rate-change applied to route:forum-search-prod -> 10% by Jordan.
Alex: For rollout, add a console flag that enables the SLI buckets for a tenant. We should gate on tenant size and opt-in so we don't run reconciliation for tiny customers.
Mira: One more thing — when we show per-model/unit economics, do we normalize to 1k tokens or show per-invocation? 
Sam: Normalize to 1k tokens makes comparisons easier. Display both numbers on hover. Also include a 'model weight' line: e.g., unquantized=1.0, 8-bit=0.45.
Jordan: Implementation note: ingestion pipeline change required: add cache_credit_applied (int), lineage_id (string, hashed), route_id, model_variant_id. Backfill job should read object storage logs and emit reconciled rows to a reconciliation table.
Mira: Can we fake it first by deriving cache_credit_applied = token_count * 0.5 rule-of-thumb to validate UI before instrumentation lands?
Alex: Yes, add an estimated flag: estimated_cache_credit=true in the proto. Dashboard should visually distinguish estimated vs reconciled numbers.
Sam: Action items: 
- Sam: PR for dashboard card design (show default effective cost, hover breakdown)
- Jordan: spec to ops for sampling bump + backfill job
- Alex: ingestion schema change and proto bump (with backward compat)
- Mira: doc copy for toggle and UX notes for PMs
ops-bot: created ticket #PLAT-8123 for reconciliation job and #PLAT-8124 for proto change
Sam: Thanks, folks. If we can land the proto + estimated UI this week we can demo to product friday. :eyes:
